extracted.intended_audience: aspiring/unrepresented authors (Australia & New Zealand) submitting to literary agents, especially Curtis Brown Australia
extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step guide for preparing and submitting a manuscript/query to Curtis Brown Australia, covering eligibility, formatting, email/query content, attachments, and readiness checks. Focused primarily on debut and unrepresented authors based in Australia/New Zealand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be based in Australia or New Zealand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curtis Brown Australia only accepts writers who are physically living in Australia or New Zealand because agents and publishers need authors to be available for local publicity (festivals, radio interviews etc.). Remote authors limit publicity opportunities and the agency expects physical availability; writers’ festivals typically do not pay international travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission windows / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Curtis Brown Australia typically accepts submissions only during March, June, and October each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents open and close submission windows to manage volume; pay close attention to their stated guidelines and timing before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded genres
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency explicitly lists genres it is not interested in (examples given: self-help and short stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit work in genres the agency has excluded — these are business decisions (often data-driven/commercial) and your manuscript will not be an exception. Move on to another agency if your genre is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete manuscript required
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have a complete manuscript for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike some US practice (where nonfiction proposals/sample chapters are common), Curtis Brown Australia expects a full manuscript so they can shop the book immediately if they love it; agents earn income from commissions and need a sellable product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting: manuscript & synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript and synopsis must be in 12 point Times New Roman, double-spaced, in a Word or PDF document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents require consistent formatting for efficiency. The agency will not convert Google Docs to Word; submit exactly as requested. Indent paragraphs and provide white space to make reading easy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email subject line content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your name, manuscript title, identify it as fiction or nonfiction, and then the genre in the email subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subject line is powerful real estate — use it to communicate key info succinctly. If your title is long, truncate or summarise it; omit subtitles in the subject line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email body (cover/query letter) length
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency asks for a maximum of 300 words for the email (cover letter / query letter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tests concision and respect for the agent's time. Include total manuscript word count in the email. Keep the cover letter tightly focused and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include total manuscript word count
rubrics_metrics.description: You must include the total word count of your manuscript in the submission email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For debut authors, declaring an excessively high word count (e.g., 120,000) is a red flag; aim to reduce length if necessary. Economic considerations make 80,000–90,000 words typical for many books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count expectations for debut authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Debut writers are strongly encouraged to reduce word count to less than 100,000 words; 80,000–90,000 words is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long manuscripts cost more to produce (printing, P&L considerations). A declared 120,000 words suggests the manuscript needs a tough edit and may lead agents to move on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant biographical information only
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only relevant biographical details in your submission; Curtis Brown Australia italicises the word 'relevant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant examples: you wrote a rural mystery and grew up on a farm; include previous writing experience, related professional life (journalist, teacher, etc.), or where you've landed since events described (for memoir). Irrelevant: childhood school prizes or unrelated minutiae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis: length and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a short synopsis — a maximum of two double-spaced pages (about 600 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A synopsis is not a blurb or marketing copy; it should be a fairly dry, chronological account of what happens, showing you can manage a book-length story. Include all spoilers (do not omit endings). Avoid summarising promotional phrases like 'a classic tale of...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample pages required
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach the first three chapters or the first 50 pages of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format these pages as requested (double-spaced, 12pt Times New Roman). Indent paragraphs and provide ample white space to make reading easy for the agent. The main thing is the quality of the writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript readiness red flags
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the listed conditions apply, you are likely not ready to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Red flags include: 'Your manuscript opens with the weather.'; 'It opens with a dream.'; 'You don’t know your genre.'; 'It’s your first draft with a spell-check.'; 'You haven’t sought a third-party (non-family member) to read your manuscript and provide constructive feedback.'; 'You can’t name any comparison or competitor titles.' If these apply, revise and seek feedback before querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous writing/publishing history
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any previous writing experience or publishing history in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not worry if you have no prior publications — many debut authors are published without them. But include blogs, newsletters, regular columns, or self-published books (even in different genres) because they are relevant credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis should demonstrate story management
rubrics_metrics.description: The synopsis must show the agent you can manage a book-length story — setting out events and consequences, cause and effect in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clinical and clear rather than promotional. The purpose is to prove structural understanding and narrative control rather than to sell with marketing language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents will not convert file types
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send a Google Doc expecting conversion; submit Word or PDF as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency will not convert files for you. Follow submission specs exactly to avoid immediate rejection or being ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing is primary
rubrics_metrics.description: The main thing is the quality of your writing — a manuscript that wows may compensate for a poor query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless, a poor query sets up the expectation of a manuscript that is not ready. Both query and manuscript matter; aim to have a strong submission packet.
